heroHeadline: Robin AI Completes First Autonomous Drug Discovery; Microsoft–Mayo Clinic Build Frontier Health Model; WHO Issues AI Policy Governance Framework
heroSubtitle: FutureHouse's Robin multi-agent AI system achieved the first documented end-to-end autonomous scientific discovery: independently identifying ripasudil (a glaucoma drug) as a dry age-related macular degeneration treatment candidate, analyzing 551 papers in 30 minutes, and confirming efficacy in lab experiments — all without human direction (Nature, June 2026). Microsoft and Mayo Clinic announced a landmark partnership on June 2 to build a frontier AI healthcare model trained on Mayo's de-identified longitudinal clinical records, owned by Mayo and licensed globally to extend Mayo expertise to underserved hospitals worldwide. The WHO published a major discussion paper on June 2 calling for algorithmic impact assessments and human-in-the-loop oversight across all AI health applications, warning that AI systems may create 'epistemic injustice' by marginalizing Indigenous knowledge and lived experience. The ITU AI for Good Impact Awards 2026 announced finalists from 300 applications across 65 countries, including WFP HungerMap Live, Indian smallholder AI credit tools, and Global South literacy platforms. A UN University report found AI data centers will consume water equivalent to 1.3 billion people's annual domestic needs by 2030, with the burden falling disproportionately on developing nations. OpenAI launched GPT-Rosalind on May 29 — a free biodefense AI for pandemic preparedness given to governments, academic labs, and NGOs, deployed with Lawrence Livermore, Johns Hopkins APL, and CEPI.
footerNote: Data sourced from peer-reviewed journals (NEJM AI, Nature, Science, The Lancet, npj Digital Medicine), UN agencies (WHO, FAO, WFP, UNESCO, ITU, UNU), and major technology research outlets. Impact claims require independent validation; contested figures are marked.
